subject: Pinebridge — streaming SLO alignment & cost playbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@pinebridge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pinebridge — streaming SLO alignment & cost playbook

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on SLOs, constraints, and the PoC scope. Appreciate Alex & Sandra jumping in.

Key requirements (from the call)
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms for a 256-token request (streaming enabled).
- Sustained throughput: ~120 req/s (steady-state); expected bursts up to 600 concurrent inflight streams.
- Typical prompt: ~80 tokens (median), but 5–10% of requests hit 512+ tokens.
- Streaming: chunked output with first-token latency prioritized (client-side needs partial tokens within 40–60ms after model emits).
- Accuracy sensitivity: some business-critical prompts (logistics planning) need higher quality — these can tolerate slightly higher latency; others (status queries) must be low-latency.

Primary cost/performance levers we discussed (what we'll validate in PoC):
- Continuous batching: target batch size ~24–48 depending on latency SLO to maximize GPU utilization without pushing p95 too high.
- Prefix/KV caching: recommend session-based KV cache TTL and warm-up for repeat prompt prefixes (expected ~30% prefix reuse).
- Quantization profiles: evaluate int8 vs 4-bit quant (LLM-4q) for the low-latency variant to quantify accuracy delta and token cost improvements.
- Model variants: two-path approach — low-latency quantized model for interactive flows, fallback to higher-accuracy fp16 model for critical prompts or when quality regressions detected.
- Autoscaling & reserved capacity: reserved pool for steady 120 req/s plus burst capacity policy for spikes to 600 concurrent streams.

Attachments I’m including for the team: slo_matrix_pinebridge.xlsx (breakdown by intent), poc_benchmark_instructions.md (how we’ll run the bench), and a short traffic sample schema.

Agreed next steps
1) Pinebridge to share a 24–72 hour traffic sample export (schema in attachment) — Sandra to send by Wed EOD.
2) Redwood to run 2 bench configurations and deliver a p95/p99 latency matrix and cost estimate:
   - Config A: low-latency quantized variant (continuous batching, batch target 32)
   - Config B: higher-accuracy fp16 variant (larger batch sizing, batching tolerant)
3) Define routing policy: intent-based routing (status queries -> low-latency path; planning -> high-accuracy path).
4) Schedule a 2-week PoC: perf runs + quality evaluation on Pinebridge's prioritized prompt set.

Action items (owners)
- Sandra: send traffic sample + confirm monthly QPS and peak concurrency windows (owner: Sandra).
- Neha: plan bench runs and confirm infra configuration (owner: Neha).
- Marissa: prepare pricing delta for Config A vs Config B and reserved capacity options (owner: Marissa).

Timeline proposal
- Traffic sample by Wed (9/15) -> bench start 9/17 -> 5 business days of perf runs -> results review 9/24.

If this looks right I’ll kick off the bench plan and loop infra with a short runbook.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer

From: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@pinebridge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Reddy <alex.reddy@pinebridge.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pinebridge — streaming SLO alignment & cost playbook

Thanks Karthik — this captures it well. A couple clarifications and a small update from our side.

Clarifications
- Our "status" intents are extremely latency sensitive and are ~60% of traffic. The planning intents are ~20% and can accept p95 up to 400ms.
- Concurrency: the 600 figure is per-region burst across our EU+US footprint. US alone sees ~420 peak.
- Security: we need PoC runs to use our customer-managed KMS keys for encryption-at-rest of logs; can you confirm that’s supported in the PoC path?

Attached is a 12-hour sample of traffic (pinebridge_traffic_sample.json) and a short table of the critical prompt set. We also added a column for "tolerance" to indicate which prompts must go to high-accuracy path.

One more ask — for streaming, the client expects partial token chunks every ~50ms after the model yields the next token. Can Redwood provide guidance on the safe batching window (in ms) to preserve that behavior? We don’t want batching to add more than 25–40ms to the first-token latency in the streaming path.

We’re ok with the 9/17 bench start. Please confirm the contact for the PoC infra ramp and whether a brief escalation path exists (SLA exception) if we observe regressions.

Sandra Lee
Head of AI & Automation | Pinebridge Logistics
sandra.lee@pinebridge.com
+1 212-555-0128

Attachment: pinebridge_traffic_sample.json (12-hour export, anonymized)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@pinebridge.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pinebridge — streaming SLO alignment & cost playbook

Looping Neha & Marissa to convert the call summary into an executable bench and pricing ask for the PoC. Forwarding Sandra's sample (attached).

Neha — please prepare two bench configs and include these checks:
- Bench A (low-latency path):
  - Model: quantized 4-bit candidate (LLM-4q) or int8 profile if 4-bit fails QA
  - Continuous batching: target batch latency window 12–18ms; target batch size 24–32 (tune to meet p95 150ms).
  - Streaming behavior: ensure chunk flush on token emission (client-side partial chunks every ~50ms) — measure first-byte latency and added batching delay.
  - KV cache: enable session-based cache with TTL 30m; measure hit-rate impact.
- Bench B (accuracy path):
  - Model: fp16 baseline variant
  - Batching: larger windows for throughput efficiency
  - Verify quality delta on prioritized prompt set — collect BLEU/ROUGE or human pass/fail samples.

Marissa — we need:
- A clear cost delta spreadsheet (per 100k tokens) for the two configs including reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) vs on-demand bursting.
- A short paragraph recommending the routing policy and failover: intent-based routing + automatic fallback to accuracy path on quality regression.

Also please confirm: PoC infra can be provisioned under Pinebridge's customer-managed KMS for logs and metrics. Sandra asked for an escalation contact; propose: Marissa (account) -> Karthik (technical) -> Neha (infra).

I’ll open HubSpot deal PB-2026-045 and attach results. Tentative bench start 2026-09-17.

Thanks —
Karthik
